newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, augurs primary fall.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, augurs primary fall.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 70 basis points at 19.70 percent on Tuesday as a heavy inflow of foreign investors paved the way for further falls in primary rates, traders said.
"Money keeps flowing in and you can see that just by looking at the exchange rate," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.4 of a centavo firmer at 7.7900/7.7935 per dollar.
"The market was bolstered mainly by foreign capital flow, which leads us to think that primary rates may fall by more than 100 basis points," another trader said.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they expected an average assignment rate of 20.30 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes at the central bank's weekly primary auction of government securities.
This would be a fall of 115 basis points since last week's auction and would take primary rates to their lowest level since the December 1994 devaluation crisis.
Some dealers did, however, express concern over the possibility of such a sharp fall in primary rates.
"If the flow of foreign capital were to keep up indefinitely, then there would be no problem, but experience shows that does not usually happen," one dealer said.
"We must be close to floor levels, but rates will stay down so long as the peso does not go awry."
Banco de Mexico is due to announce the results of its weekly primary auction at 1830 local time.

Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed down 20 basis points at 21.70 percent. Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity by draining 5.711 billion pesos from the market through five secondary market auctions.
Liquidity of 311 million pesos was scheduled to return to the market from prior central bank participation.
